name: the Philippines
heroAlt: Campus of a partner medical university in the Philippines
tagline: Four NMC-aligned partner universities, an American-model MD curriculum taught entirely in English, and clinical exposure designed to strengthen practical understanding and support FMGE preparation.
intro: The Philippines has taught medicine in English for over seventy years, on a curriculum built to the American model. For an Indian student that means no language barrier, a pathway that must satisfy the applicable NMC FMGL requirements for Indian registration, and clinical training in genuinely busy hospitals.

why.title: A curriculum built for the FMGE
Hospitals with real patient volume
points: Affiliated hospitals with large bed capacity

why.title: Four campuses, one honest recommendation
points: Honest recommendation, even if none fit

clinical.intro: Across our four Philippine partners, students rotate through affiliated hospitals with several thousand beds between them, beginning patient contact in the early years rather than in the final ones.

phases.title: Pre-medicine
phases.text: Foundation sciences, medical terminology, clinical orientation and English communication. Required at some of our Philippine partners, not all.

phases.title: Doctor of Medicine
phases.text: Anatomy through pharmacology, then clinical clerkship across the major departments, with FMGE preparation running alongside.

phases.title: Internship
phases.text: A supervised hospital internship where the university and local registration require one. Whether it sits inside the 4.5 years or extends past them differs by university.

duration: The exact structure differs by university, so we will not quote one figure for all four. DMSF states 6.5 years in total including the internship. Gullas states one year of pre-medicine followed by 4.5 years of medical studies. Your counsellor will confirm the current pathway, and the internship requirement, for whichever university you choose.

name: Timor-Leste
heroAlt: Campus of a partner medical university in Timor-Leste
tagline: Two NMC-aligned partner universities in Dili, English-medium teaching, and a lower total cost than most routes into medicine abroad.
intro: Timor-Leste is a younger destination than the Philippines and a smaller one, which is exactly why it suits some students better. Class sizes are small, the cost is lower, and the teaching is in English.

why.title: Both campuses in Dili
points: No need to travel between cities

why.title: The honest trade-off
points: A new environment to adapt to

clinical.intro: Students at both Dili universities train in the country's main referral and regional hospitals, with supervised patient contact through the clinical years and an internship before graduation.

phases.title: Medical studies
phases.text: A curriculum patterned on the Indian MBBS and taught in English, with clinical rotations through the Dili hospitals.

phases.title: Rotational internship
phases.text: A supervised internship across emergency, critical care, wards, operation theatres and rural health centres.

duration: Both Dili universities state 4.5 years of medical study followed by a 12-month internship, so 5.5 years in total. There is no separate pre-medicine year, which is where the Timor-Leste route differs from the Philippine one.
